newsitem.title: USA: American General deal won by Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: American General deal won by Morgan Stanley.

text.p: American General Corp issued $500 million in capital securities via a competive 144A private placement offering won by Morgan Stanley & Co, market sources said.
The deal, which has a 49-year maturity was won by Morgan Stanley at a spread of 126.7 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, according to several market sources.
One market source said Morgan Stanley was offering the securities to investors at a spread of 123 basis points over Treasuries.
Morgan Stanley declined to comment on the deal.
Other players speculated that a 123 basis points bid was unrealistically rich and that the underwriter would most likely revise the offer.
Sources noted that, if the initial offering price is to high the underwriters will terminate the offering and set prices with individual investors on a negotiated basis.
The competitive bid was initially slated for 1100 EST/1600 GMT, but was delayed until late afternoon, sources said.
Standard & Poor's assigned American General's offering an A-plus rating on Tuesday, while simultaneously keeping it under review for a possible downgrade.
Standard & Poor's expects the proceeds from the offering to be used for debt repayment and general corporate purposes.
S&P said American General and its units, and the senior unsecured debt rating of American General Finance Corp, remain under review for a possible downgrade, where they were placed February 13.
American General Corp could not be reached for comment.
